newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot prods ease after API despite stock draws.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot prods ease after API despite stock draws.

text.p: U.S. spot products prices slumped mildly in late afternoon dealings after the American Petroleum Institute released its weekly inventory report, industry sources said.
Heating oil prices eased by about 0.15 cent a gallon from from late afternoon assessments, while unleaded gasoline fell by less than one-tenth of one cent.

In its weekly report, API said heating oil stocks rose by about 400,000 barrels in both the total U.S. and on the East Coast. But the rise still left the nation nearly 20 million barrels behind year-ago levels.
U.S. low sulphur stocks fell by 880,000 barrels, but managed a 293,000 barrel gain in the midwest region.
API reported a seasonably normal gasoline draw of 2.2 million barrels. East Coast stocks fell by 2.67 million despite a hefty jump in national imports and output.
Before the data, spot prices were mixed in thin talk.

They attributed the slack activity level to the expiration of August product's contracts on Friday and to general late-summer malaise. Hurricane Edouard continued to move toward the U.S. East Coast. But experts predict that it will not be a threat to business interests at least until the weekend.
-- Franklin Paul, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
